message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Seven credible, newly surfaced vulnerabilities match the monitored NGINX product family: five in NGINX Open Source/Plus and two in its optional njs module. NGINX rates all seven **Medium**. The five core issues are configuration-dependent; no exploitation was reported by NGINX/F5 in the reviewed sources. One newly published WordPress-plugin issue is listed separately because the inventory names WordPress but does not confirm that plugin is installed.

**Scope:** `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only, combined and deduplicated. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-14 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-15 23:40 UTC (2026-10-15 05:10 IST through 2026-10-16 05:10 IST).

### Findings

**CVE-2026-15176 — NGINX alias/rewrite buffer overflow**
- **Product:** NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Crafted requests can trigger a heap buffer overflow when `alias`, `rewrite`, and `$request_filename` are used in specific combinations, causing worker restart and potentially code execution under additional conditions.
- **Relevance:** Nginx is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

**CVE-2026-93479 — NGINX script-evaluation buffer overflow**
- **Product:** NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Certain regex `map` capture uses can overflow a worker-process buffer, with possible denial of service or code execution depending on configuration.
- **Relevance:** Nginx is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

**CVE-2026-95101 — NGINX HTTP/3 request-body injection**
- **Product:** NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** With HTTP/3 and request buffering enabled, a client can inject extra bytes into a proxied request or bypass the configured request-body size limit.
- **Relevance:** Nginx is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

**CVE-2026-97629 — NGINX TLS session forgery**
- **Product:** NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Automatic TLS session-ticket key rotation with a shared session cache can permit non-deterministic session forgery and possible bypass of client-certificate verification.
- **Relevance:** Nginx is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

**CVE-2026-97205 — NGINX AIO use-after-free**
- **Product:** NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus
- **Severity:** Medium (NGINX rating)
- **Description:** Asynchronous file I/O used with SSI can cause a worker-process use-after-free, leading to a crash, memory corruption, or possible code execution in affected configurations.
- **Relevance:** Nginx is explicitly monitored.
- **Source:** [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

**CVE-2026-101025 — njs malformed-XML memory exhaustion**
- **Product:** NGINX njs module
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Description:** Repeated parsing of malformed XML can leak memory and exhaust an NGINX worker process.
- **Relevance:** njs is an official NGINX module; exposure requires that the module and affected XML processing are in use.
- **Source:** [NGINX njs security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/docs/njs/security.html)

**CVE-2026-101019 — njs inconsistent XML attribute handling**
- **Product:** NGINX njs module
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Description:** Entity references in XML attributes can produce inconsistent values and affect signed-XML validation.
- **Relevance:** njs is an official NGINX module; exposure requires that the module and affected XML processing are in use.
- **Source:** [NGINX njs security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/docs/njs/security.html)

### Possible matches needing review

**CVE-2026-3712 — PhastPress WordPress plugin SSRF**
- **Product:** PhastPress plugin for WordPress
- **Severity:** High (CVSS 3.1: 7.3)
- **Description:** PhastPress through 3.10 allows unauthenticated server-side request forgery through a Host-header-based whitelist bypass.
- **Why uncertain:** WordPress is monitored, but the supplied inventory does not show whether PhastPress is installed.
- **Source:** [CVE record](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-3712)

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

A dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, MongoDB-owned advisories, CVE/NVD records, GitHub Security Advisories, and CISA sources. No credible MongoDB-family vulnerability was newly reported within this run's window. [MongoDB Alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts)

### Review priority

Prompt review is recommended for NGINX deployments. Confirm the running NGINX version and whether the affected directives/modules are enabled; versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 are listed as not vulnerable for the five core issues, and njs 1.0.2 is listed as not vulnerable for the two njs issues. Also verify whether the PhastPress plugin is present on any monitored WordPress instance.
